1.title: Availability Zones, Availability Sets and Scale Sets
1.text: Welcome to Module nine: Availability Zones, Availability Sets and Scale Sets. It covers the exam area Deploy and manage Azure compute resources. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Deploy virtual machines to availability zones and availability sets. Deploy and configure Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources (twenty-twenty-five percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft Learn A Z-one hundred four study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-six, two thousand twenty-three.

1.title: Why availability options
1.text: Why availability options. A single V M can fail from hardware faults or planned maintenance. Azure offers placement options so some instances stay up.

1.title: Why availability options, continued
1.text: Why availability options. The figure shows this: Availability zones, and fault and update domains in an availability set.

1.title: Why availability options, continued
1.text: Why availability options. Single V M with Premium S S D disks. Protects against: Little. V M S L A (typical): ninety-nine point nine percent. Availability set. Protects against: Rack and maintenance failures inside one datacenter. V M S L A (typical): ninety-nine point nine five percent. Availability zones. Protects against: A whole datacenter (zone) failure. V M S L A (typical): ninety-nine point nine nine percent. S L A percentages.

1.title: Availability zones
1.text: Availability zones. An availability zone is a physically separate location (own power, cooling, network) within a region. Regions that support zones have at least three. Zonal service. You pick the zone for a V M, disk or I P (for example zone one). Zone-redundant service. Azure spreads automatically across zones (for example zone-redundant storage, Standard load balancer). Set at creation. A V M's zone is chosen when you create it; to change it you recreate it.

1.title: Availability sets
1.text: Availability sets. An availability set places V Ms across fault domains and update domains in one datacenter. Fault domain. A group sharing power and network (a rack); V Ms spread across up to three. Update domain. A group rebooted together during planned maintenance; up to twenty.

1.title: Availability sets, continued
1.text: Availability sets. You choose the set when creating the V M; you cannot add an existing V M to a set (recreate it). Put each tier (web, app) in its own set behind a load balancer. Exam tip: Zones protect against datacenter failure; availability sets protect against rack and maintenance events inside a datacenter. A V M cannot be in both a zone and an availability set.

1.title: Virtual Machine Scale Sets
1.text: Virtual Machine Scale Sets. A Virtual Machine Scale Set (V M S S) deploys and manages a group of identical, load-balanced V Ms that can scale out and in automatically. Autoscale. Rules on metrics (for example C P U above seventy percent for ten minutes: add two instances) or schedules. Limits. Set minimum, maximum and default instance counts. Scale out or in. Add or remove instances (horizontal). Orchestration modes. Flexible (recommended, mixes V M types, spread across zones) and Uniform (identical instances).

1.title: Virtual Machine Scale Sets, continued
1.text: Virtual Machine Scale Sets. Load balancing. Use an Azure Load Balancer or Application Gateway in front. Health and repair. Health probes and automatic instance repairs. Updates. Upgrade policy (automatic, rolling, manual) updates the model and the instances. Exam tip: Pick zones for datacenter failure, availability sets for rack and maintenance, scale sets for automatic capacity; do not combine a zone with an availability set.

1.title: Virtual Machine Scale Sets, continued
1.text: Virtual Machine Scale Sets. The figure shows this: A scale set behind a load balancer, with autoscale rules adding and removing instances. Exam tip: "Add V Ms automatically when C P U is high and remove them when load drops" equals Virtual Machine Scale Set with autoscale rules.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A workload must survive the failure of an entire datacenter in the region. What should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Availability zones. Zones are separate datacenters in the region.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. V Ms must be protected from rack failures and planned maintenance in one datacenter. What should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: An availability set. Fault and update domains protect against those events.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An existing V M must be added to an availability set. What is the correct action? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Recreate the V M in the availability set. A V M can only be placed in a set when it is created.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A web tier should add instances automatically when C P U exceeds seventy percent. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Virtual Machine Scale Set with autoscale. Scale sets support metric-based autoscale.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. What is a fault domain? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A group of V Ms sharing power and network, such as a rack. Fault domains share hardware infrastructure.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which option gives the highest typical V M availability S L A? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Availability zones. Zones provide ninety-nine point nine nine percent.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does an availability zone protect against? Answer: The failure of a whole datacenter. Question two. What is an update domain? Answer: A group of V Ms rebooted together during planned maintenance. Question three. How many fault domains can an availability set use? Answer: Up to three.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What triggers autoscale in a scale set? Answer: Metric rules or schedules. Question five. Which orchestration mode is recommended? Answer: Flexible. Question six. Can a V M be in an availability set and a zone? Answer: No.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Zones: separate datacenters, ninety-nine point nine nine percent, chosen at creation. Availability sets: fault plus update domains, ninety-nine point nine five percent, chosen at creation. Scale sets: identical V Ms, autoscale by metric or schedule, flexible mode, health repair.
